planting.note: Plant dormant canes or containerized transplants in early spring, spacing widely and installing a sturdy multi-wire trellis, since the long trailing canes will not support themselves.

directions: Marion is the trailing blackberry that put Oregon berry breeding on the map, released in 1956 from a 1945 USDA cross of 'Chehalem' and 'Olallie' and named for the county where it was first field-trialed. Its long, thorny canes need a sturdy trellis but reward the extra work with small, deeply complex, wine-toned berries prized by processors and bakers well above most modern thornless cultivars. Marion's superior flavor became the benchmark that later thornless USDA-ARS releases like Black Diamond, Black Pearl, and Nightfall were bred to approach without the thorns. Cut spent floricanes to the ground after harvest and train the current season's primocanes onto the wires for next year's crop.
sources: Oregon State University Extension — Caneberry Production Guide

planting.note: Repot into fresh bark mix in spring after the fall-to-winter bloom cycle finishes, dividing congested pseudobulb clumps.

directions: John Banks is an Australian-bred Zygopetalum grex known for producing green sepals and petals densely overlaid with chocolate-maroon barring around a violet-blue-veined lip, a color combination that has made it a workhorse parent in modern Zygopetalum breeding. Established plants send up fragrant, heavily hyacinth-scented spikes from the base of the current pseudobulb in fall and winter. Grow in intermediate to cool temperatures with medium to bright light in an open, well-drained bark mix, keeping the roots evenly moist since Zygopetalum has no thick water-storing pseudobulb reserve. It was crossed with 'B.G. White' to create the taller, larger-flowered hybrid 'Titanic', among many other modern Zygopetalum introductions tracing back to this parent.

planting.note: Repot into fresh bark mix in spring after the fall-to-winter bloom cycle finishes, dividing congested pseudobulb clumps.

directions: B.G. White is an Australian-bred Zygopetalum grex valued for a paler, more white-based flower than most of the genus, with fine maroon-purple barring over cream-white sepals and petals and a white lip washed in blue-purple veining. It shares the strong, sweet hyacinth fragrance typical of the genus and blooms from the base of a newly matured pseudobulb in fall and winter. Culture matches other Zygopetalum: intermediate to cool temperatures, medium-bright light, and a bark-based mix kept evenly moist rather than allowed to dry out between waterings. Crossed with 'John Banks', it produced the taller-spiked hybrid 'Titanic', reflecting its continuing role as breeding stock for paler-toned modern Zygopetalum hybrids.

planting.note: Grow in a medium pot or basket with coarse bark in bright, filtered light; Bracdiana is a vigorous, free-flowering hybrid that tolerates more cultural variation than many Brassia species.

directions: Bracdiana is one of the most widely distributed Brassia hybrids in general cultivation, prized for long, tapering, yellow-green sepals and petals heavily barred in chocolate-brown spots on a spidery flower that can approach eight inches across. Its strong, sweet fragrance and free-flowering habit on a relatively compact plant have made it a standard entry point into spider orchid growing for decades. Provide bright, filtered light in a well-drained bark mix, watering freely through active growth and allowing a slight dry-down between waterings, especially in cooler months. It has been used repeatedly as breeding stock for more compact modern Brassia hybrids, including 'Eternal Wind'.
sources: American Orchid Society — Brassia culture sheet
Royal Horticultural Society International Orchid Register — Brassia grex registrations

planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in spring in well-drained, dry to average soil in full sun; give plants several weeks of direct sun after any time indoors to restore full leaf color.

directions: Carnival is a Walters Gardens Mangave selection carrying a bold cream-to-yellow blush through the center of each leaf, framed by a contrasting dark green margin — the mirror image of the green-centered, yellow-edged pattern seen on the related sport 'Kaleidoscope'. Like other Mangaves it combines Manfreda's fast, forgiving growth with Agave's tidy rosette form, reaching a garden-worthy clump in a few seasons rather than the decade-plus a true agave needs. Purple-red speckling develops across the leaf surface under strong sun and intensifies with drought stress, fading if the plant spends an extended period indoors or in low light. Grow in fast-draining, mineral-rich soil in full sun and let it dry between waterings, since Mangave rots quickly in soggy conditions.

common_name: Painted Lady Blushing Bromeliad (Variegated Neoregelia carolinae)

planting.note: Grow in a shallow pot of well-draining bromeliad mix or mount epiphytically in bright, filtered shade; keep the central cup topped with water and flush it every couple of weeks.

directions: Painted Lady is an older, widely distributed variegated selection of blushing bromeliad, its leaves banded lengthwise in cream to pale yellow against green, with the whole rosette center flushing bright red as the plant approaches bloom. It shares the species' broad, spineless-to-lightly-toothed rosette and forms offsets readily, making it easy to share out established clumps. Grow in bright, filtered light in a chunky, fast-draining bromeliad mix, keeping the central water-holding cup topped up and flushed periodically to prevent stagnation. It has long been used as breeding stock for named Neoregelia hybrids, including as a parent of 'Morado'.
sources: Bromeliad Society International — Neoregelia culture notes

planting.note: Detach rooted basal offsets from the tubular rosette and pot into a loose, fast-draining bromeliad mix.

directions: Ed McWilliams is a tubular Billbergia hybrid valued in breeding circles for heavily silver-white blotched and banded foliage layered over the vase-shaped, upright form typical of the genus. Like other Billbergia it flowers briefly but showily, sending a pendant spike of pink-bracted, blue-tipped blooms from the central tube, usually with little warning before the display fades within days. Grow in bright, filtered light in a coarse, fast-draining bark-based mix, keeping the central tube topped with fresh water and letting the roots dry somewhat between waterings. It was crossed with 'Domingos Martins' to produce the popular hybrid 'Hallelujah', among other modern Billbergia introductions drawing on its heavily marked foliage.

planting.note: Divide congested rhizome clumps in spring as new growth resumes, ensuring each division keeps healthy roots attached.

directions: Network is a selection of mosaic calathea bred for an unusually tight, uniform grid of fine light and dark green lines across each leaf, a crisper, more geometric take on the looser checkerboard pattern of the wild species. The intricate, closely woven veining reads as a distinct textural pattern rather than the blotches or bold bands typical of most other prayer plants, making it a strong contrast plant next to broader-patterned Goeppertia. Grow in deep shade to bright indirect light in consistently moist, humus-rich soil with humidity above 50 percent, since dry air quickly browns the thin leaf edges. Water with rainwater or distilled water rather than tap water, since mineral buildup shows up quickly as scorch on the fine leaf margins.

planting.note: Divide congested rhizome clumps in spring as new growth resumes, ensuring each division keeps healthy roots attached.

directions: Medallion is among the most widely sold houseplant cultivars in the genus, its broad, rounded leaves marked with alternating concentric bands of dark and light green radiating out from the midrib like a painted medal, with a solid wine-purple reverse. The bold, symmetrical pattern reads clearly even in modest light, which along with its relatively forgiving nature has made it a mainstay of big-box and grocery-store houseplant sections. Grow in bright indirect to medium shade with consistently moist, humus-rich soil and humidity above 50 percent, watering with rainwater or distilled water to avoid the leaf-edge browning that tap water minerals cause. It is also the wild-type-adjacent parent behind newer, more dramatically banded roseopicta selections such as 'Dottie' and 'Corona'.

planting.note: Divide congested rhizome clumps in spring as new growth resumes, ensuring each division keeps healthy roots attached.

directions: Corona layers a soft rose-pink band inside a silvery outer ring around each leaf center, giving roseopicta's typical concentric pattern a halo-like, two-tone glow that sets it apart from the crisper single-color banding of 'Medallion'. The broad, oval leaves carry the same deep maroon-purple reverse typical of the group, and the plant forms a tidy, medium-sized clumping rosette well suited to a tabletop or grouped shade planting. Grow in bright indirect light with consistently moist, humus-rich soil and humidity above 50 percent, since dry air and strong sun both fade the pink banding. Water with rainwater or distilled water, as with other roseopicta selections, to prevent mineral scorch along the leaf margins.

planting.note: Divide congested rhizome clumps in spring as new growth resumes, ensuring each division keeps healthy roots and several leaves attached.

directions: White Fusion is a hybrid calathea prized, and notoriously expensive when first introduced, for irregular splashes of white, cream, and soft green across each leaf, with fine purple pencil-striping on the reverse that shows through faintly on the leaf's upper surface. Because the white tissue carries little chlorophyll, it grows more slowly and is markedly less forgiving of low humidity or mineral-rich water than solid-green prayer plants, developing crisp brown edges quickly if conditions slip. Grow in bright indirect light with consistently moist, humus-rich soil and humidity ideally above 60 percent, watering only with rainwater, distilled water, or water left open overnight to dissipate chlorine and minerals. Its reputation as one of the fussier houseplant Goeppertia hybrids has not dented its enduring popularity among variegated-plant collectors.

planting.note: Plant bare-root while dormant in late winter or early spring, choosing a site with full sun and deep, well-drained soil.

directions: Late Santa Rosa is a later-ripening sport of the classic Santa Rosa Japanese plum, carrying the same reddish-purple skin and juicy, aromatic amber flesh but extending the harvest window several weeks beyond the standard cultivar. This makes it useful for orchards and home gardens that already grow Santa Rosa and want to stretch fresh plum season rather than concentrate the whole crop at once. Culture is identical to the parent cultivar: plant in deep, well-drained loam in full sun, and though partially self-fruitful, plant a second Japanese plum nearby for a heavier, more reliable set. Prune to an open-center vase shape in the dormant season and thin heavy fruit sets to 4-6 inches apart to improve size and reduce limb breakage.

common_name: Laxton's Progress Pea (Early English Heirloom Shelling Pea)

planting.note: Direct sow 1-1.5 inches deep as soon as the ground can be worked in spring; the short, sturdy vines need only light twiggy support.

directions: Laxton's Progress is an early-maturing English heirloom shelling pea bred by the historic Laxton Brothers nursery, valued for its short, sturdy vines and heavy set of well-filled pods on plants that need only light support. It was one of the two parent lines, alongside 'Perfection', that USDA breeders crossed in 1943 to create the heat-tolerant modern classic 'Wando'. Direct-sow into cool, workable spring soil as early as the ground can be prepared, since like all garden peas it grows and yields best well ahead of summer heat. The dwarf, self-supporting habit suits raised beds and smaller gardens where taller vining peas would need substantial trellising.

common_name: Loxton Lass Tomato (Orange Beefsteak Dwarf Tomato)

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost; the compact, dwarf-indeterminate habit suits raised beds and large containers.

directions: Loxton Lass bears smooth, oblate orange beefsteak fruit with the same well-balanced, rich flavor as its sibling release Loxton Lad, but on a noticeably smaller-fruited plant. It shares the same origin as Loxton Lad: a 2009 cross of Rosella Purple and an unnamed orange heirloom made by Patrina Nuske Small, stabilized by Dwarf Tomato Project volunteers and released as an OSSI-pledged variety. Start seeds indoors 4-6 weeks before the last frost and transplant into fertile, well-drained soil, staking the sturdy, rugose-leafed stems lightly for support. Harvest as fruit ripens fully on the vine for the sweetest flavor.

planting.note: Grow basket- or slab-mounted with roots exposed to air; repot or remount only as the mounting medium breaks down.

directions: Kasem's Delight is a Thailand-bred strap-leaf Vanda hybrid known for producing richly saturated blue-to-violet, tessellated flowers on a relatively compact plant compared with full-size species Vanda. It has been used repeatedly as parent stock in modern strap-leaf Vanda breeding programs aiming to concentrate deep, saturated color onto more manageable plants, including as one parent of the award-generating hybrid 'Robert's Delight'. Grow in a slatted basket or mounted with roots exposed to air, in strong light and high humidity typical of Vanda-alliance culture. Water or mist daily in warm weather, letting the exposed roots dry briefly between soakings to prevent rot.

planting.note: Divide and repot after bloom finishes, once new growth is underway, in a bark-and-perlite mix.

directions: Miretta is a Cymbidium hybrid grex known chiefly today as a parent behind the compact, fragrant 'Peter Pan' grex, contributing to a plant far smaller and better suited to windowsill culture than standard large-flowered Cymbidium hybrids. It shares the more modest growth habit and freer-flowering tendency found in Cymbidium ensifolium-influenced breeding lines rather than the bulkier, cooler-growing standard Cymbidium hybrids bred mainly for cut flowers. Grow cool with bright, filtered light, watering regularly through the growing season and allowing a modest dry-down between waterings in winter. Provide an autumn day-night temperature drop to help trigger reliable spike initiation, as with other Cymbidium hybrids in its breeding line.

planting.note: Root softwood cuttings in early summer or set out container-grown plants in well-drained soil in full sun; this cultivar blooms on old wood, so prune immediately after flowering rather than in fall or winter.

directions: Snowmound is the classic, widely planted Nippon spirea cultivar against which newer, more compact selections like 'Halward's Silver' are typically measured, forming a dense, gracefully arching mound of fine, blue-green foliage. In late spring its arching stems disappear beneath a heavy, even cover of small white button-like flowers in the same lace-like display typical of the species, though on a plant that reliably reaches full shrub size rather than staying dwarf. It tolerates heat, drought, and a range of soils once established, asking only for full sun and decent drainage to perform reliably for decades with minimal care. Shear lightly right after flowering, since it blooms on old wood and sets next year's buds soon after the spring flush finishes.
